accuracy.evidence: Checked against the Met Office cloud guide (ten main types; cumulus heaped with flat bases and fair weather when small; stratus a low grey layer giving dull weather and drizzle, fog being stratus at ground level; cirrus high, wispy, made of ice crystals; cumulonimbus tall and dark with heavy showers and thunder) and NC 2013 Y4 States of matter (evaporation and condensation in the water cycle). Formation stated as damp air rising and cooling so water vapour condenses into droplets; adult text adds expansion with falling pressure and the dew point. Vapour is called invisible; cloud is liquid drops or ice. The lab's temperature falls with height (20°C to about 6°C) as a simplified lapse. Parameterised items checked at corners: p2 a-b 6..22, p4 a+b 2..7, m6 a+b 60..95 hundred metres (cirrus at 6 to 9.5 km), m7 a-b 1..12.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented children's ideas about clouds and condensation (Russell, Harlen and Watt 1989, SPACE Evaporation and Condensation; Henriques 2002 on children's weather misconceptions): clouds are steam, smoke or cotton (prediction 2, CQ steam/smoke, p1), clouds are visible water vapour (CQ vapour, m9), clouds form when air warms (prediction 1 'gets hotter', letting the bubble sink makes the cloud vanish, CQ warm/still, m1), clouds are bags holding water (m3), every cloud brings rain (forecast step, CQ allrain), cirrus are water drops (high/low sort, CQ drops), dark clouds are dirty (CQ dirty, m8).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagcloud is about how clouds form and how to tell the three basic genera apart: a draggable air bubble that becomes a cloud only above a cold-enough line and clears again when it sinks, a zoom into droplets that merge into a falling raindrop, a high-icy versus low-watery sort, drawn cumulus, stratus, cirrus and cumulonimbus skies to name, and a sky-to-forecast match. flagevap covers evaporation and the water-cycle loop; flagwxtype sorts sunny, rainy, cloudy and windy days without cloud genera. Max 6-shingle similarity 1.9%.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner sees the cause before it is named: the temperature tag drops as the bubble rises and the dashed outline turns into a white cloud exactly at the line, then vanishes again below it; zooming shows dots, not fluff, and only after three merges is a drop heavy enough to fall; wrong sorts explain liquid versus ice by height; naming uses the Latin meanings (heap, layer, curl of hair) stated in the step text and shown in the drawings.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions with tempting wrong options disproved on screen: rising vapour 'gets hotter' or 'turns into smoke' (it cools and condenses into drops), a cloud is 'steam like from a kettle' (zoom shows cold droplets), a flat grey sheet is 'cirrus' or 'cumulus' (the drawn stratus), and cirrus 'will rain on you now' (the forecast step says dry now, may change).

challenge_feedback.evidence: oops() has ten distinct messages (steam, vapour, warm, still, drops, smoke, cu, ci, allrain, dirty), each naming the wrong idea and the correction, e.g. 'Water vapour is a gas you cannot see. A cloud is the drops it turns into.' In-lab wrong answers are specific too: each misnamed sky describes the chosen genus, each wrong forecast explains what that sky really brings, each wrong high/low sort explains liquid or ice.

readability.evidence: validate_lessons passes for the family audience: kid FK 1.9, adult FK 8.4. Kid text defines water vapour, condensation and each cloud name in plain words; key terms are repeated in the lab buttons and labels.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes (no banned phrases; explanation overlap under 12% with Evaporation and the Water Cycle and Types of Weather). Kid paragraphs: how a cloud forms; drops to rain; the three types; clouds as weather clues. Adult paragraphs: curriculum and key words; named mistakes; the physics behind rising air cooling; what the lab does.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots after Show me on every step at 360 px Android (light) and iPhone 13 (dark). First pass had white cirrus on a pale sky and the bubble's temperature tag covering the cold-enough label; fixed with a deeper sky blue, darker wisp outlines and the tag moved left of the bubble. Droplet zoom redrawn with 60 drops so the merge is visible. Forecast buttons stack below the canvas at 360 px.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button ('Lift the bubble of damp air higher', 'Make the tiny drops bump and join', 'Put this cloud high up, made of ice', 'This cloud is Stratus', 'Forecast: Heavy showers, maybe thunder'). voice() updates the canvas aria-label and narration after each action. walk.cjs: desktop and iPhone 13 complete all 5 tasks with Show me, the challenge shows, axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes, no console errors.
